newsitem.title: USA: Republicans question Huang's security check.
newsitem.headline: Republicans question Huang's security check.

text.p: John Huang, suspended as a fundraiser by the Democrat Party after reports he unlawfully solicited contributions, was given a security clearance at the Commerce Department without sufficient background checks, House of Representatives Republican aides said on Wednesday.

Huang was suspended as a Democratic Party fundraiser after reports that he unlawfully solicited campaign contributions from a South Korean company. He worked for the Lippo Group of Indonesia before becoming a deputy assistant commerce secretary from mid-1994 through 1995.
He received the top secret security clearance in 1994 without any check on his work in Asia, the staff aides said.

While he was with Lippo, Huang worked in Hong Kong for the Hong Kong Chinese Bank, jointly owned by Lippo and a company owned by the Chinese government, Republican staff of the House International Relations Committee told reporters.

"There was no overseas component in his (Huang's) background check. It appears that what was done was the bare minimum," said one staffer, who asked that his name not be used. He said a foreign background check on Huang was requested but never performed.

"It's very strange. What is wrong with the Commerce Department? What is wrong with the administration?" the staffer asked. He said the lack of a foreign background check raised security concerns, although there was no evidence that Huang compromised classified information.

In his government position, Huang got a weekly security briefing and had access to classified material, the staffers said. They said he was born in China, grew up in Taiwan and became a naturalised U.S. citizen in 1976.

They released a Jan. 31, 1994, Commerce Department memo that gave Huang a waiver for an interim top secret clearance until a background investigation could be completed. The memo stated, "Huang is granted this waiver due to the critical need for his expertise in the new administration for Secretary (Ron) Brown."
Huang did not join the department until July 1994 and got his permanent security clearance that October.
The International Affairs Committee and the House Intelligence Committee are asking the administration for more information on Huang's security clearance.

Huang on Tuesday was questioned by lawyers for Judicial Watch, a conservative legal group that is suing the Commerce Department claiming Brown used foreign trade missions to improperly raise funds for Democrats.
